scenes.title: 开头
scenes.text: Pressure. Anxiety. What comes to mind? Something you are going through, or someone close to you? Or a tension that has lasted so long, you can never quite let it go?
scenes.text_zh: 谈到压力？焦虑？你想到什么？自己，或者身边的人，正在经历的一段日子？还是一种持续了很久、总也放不下的紧绷？
scenes.voice_spoken: Pressure. Anxiety. What comes to mind? Something you are going through, or someone close to you? Or a tension that has lasted so long, you can never quite let it go?

scenes.title: 开头
scenes.text: When you think of Chopin, or Romanticism, what comes to mind? Lyricism, delicacy, a chance to drift away? The grandeur and beauty of nature? A longing for freedom, revolution, resistance? What is romantic about Romanticism? And what does it have to do with pressure and anxiety? Today, through Chopin's music and the work of several Romantic painters, we will explore those questions. And stay for a small surprise at the end.
scenes.text_zh: 谈到肖邦，谈到浪漫主义，你想到什么？抒情，细腻，放空，自然的崇高与绮丽？向往自由，革命，抗争？什么是浪漫主义的浪漫？和压力与焦虑有什么关系，今天让我们藉着肖邦的音乐和几位浪漫主义画家了解一下浪漫主义，结尾还有小彩蛋，不要放过哦。
scenes.voice_spoken: When you think of Chopin, or Romanticism, what comes to mind? Lyricism, delicacy, a chance to drift away? The grandeur and beauty of nature? A longing for freedom, revolution, resistance? What is romantic about Romanticism? And what does it have to do with pressure and anxiety? Today, through Chopin's music and the work of several Romantic painters, we will explore those questions. And stay for a small surprise at the end.

scenes.title: 开头
scenes.text: First, let's listen to ten seconds of Chopin.
scenes.text_zh: 我们先听十秒肖邦...
scenes.voice_spoken: First, let's listen to ten seconds of Chopin.

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: It sounds peaceful, doesn't it? Can you imagine that, during the winter when Chopin worked on these preludes, he sometimes played in a state of profound grief and anxiety?
scenes.text_zh: 听起来很平静，对吧？你能想象，写这些前奏曲的那个冬天，肖邦曾在极度悲伤和焦虑中弹琴吗？
scenes.voice_spoken: It sounds peaceful, doesn't it? Can you imagine that, during the winter when Chopin worked on these preludes, he sometimes played in a state of profound grief and anxiety?

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: In 1838, Chopin and the writer George Sand arrived on the island of Mallorca with her two children. At first, he wrote that the sky was like turquoise, and the mountains like emeralds. Then winter brought rain, and his health grew worse. They moved into an old monastery.
scenes.text_zh: 1838 年，肖邦和作家乔治·桑带着她的两个孩子到了马略卡岛。刚到时，他写信说，那里的天像绿松石，山像祖母绿。入冬后，雨多了，他的身体也更差了。他们搬进那里的一座旧修道院。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1838, Chopin and the writer George Sand arrived on the island of Mallorca with her two children. At first, he wrote that the sky was like turquoise, and the mountains like emeralds. Then winter brought rain, and his health grew worse. They moved into an old monastery.

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: One evening, George Sand went out for supplies and was caught in a violent storm. She did not return to the monastery until late at night. When she opened the door, she found Chopin at the piano, pale, his gaze unfocused, absorbed in a state somewhere between waking and dreaming.
scenes.text_zh: 有一晚，乔治·桑出门采购被暴雨困住，深夜才赶回修道院。她推开门，发现肖邦正坐在钢琴前演奏，脸色苍白，眼神迷离，完全沉浸在一种近乎梦游的半清醒状态中。
scenes.voice_spoken: One evening, George Sand went out for supplies and was caught in a violent storm. She did not return to the monastery until late at night. When she opened the door, she found Chopin at the piano, pale, his gaze unfocused, absorbed in a state somewhere between waking and dreaming.

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: When Chopin saw her, he cried out: Ah, I knew it. You were dead! Then he told her how, as he played, he had gradually slipped into a dreamlike vision. He had imagined himself dead, lying at the bottom of an icy lake. Cold, heavy drops of water were falling on his chest, one by one, with relentless regularity.
scenes.text_zh: 肖邦看到她时惊呼了一声, 说：“啊，我就知道，你们已经死了！”，随后告诉她，自己在弹琴时渐渐陷入了沉睡般的幻觉。他梦见自己已经死去，沉在冰冷的湖底，而冰冷、沉重的水滴正一滴一滴、极有规律地落在他的胸口上。
scenes.voice_spoken: When Chopin saw her, he cried out: Ah, I knew it. You were dead! Then he told her how, as he played, he had gradually slipped into a dreamlike vision. He had imagined himself dead, lying at the bottom of an icy lake. Cold, heavy drops of water were falling on his chest, one by one, with relentless regularity.

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: When Sand asked him to listen to the rain falling from the eaves, Chopin denied that he was imitating the sounds of nature. Yet the insistent repeated note in this D-flat major prelude can sound like a pulse, or water that will never stop dripping. The work is now commonly known as the Raindrop Prelude.
scenes.text_zh: 当乔治·桑让他听听窗外屋檐上的雨声时，肖邦否认自己是在模仿大自然的雨滴。然而，这首降D大调前奏曲全曲贯穿的持续低音重复，就像永不停歇的脉搏或滴水声，后人也因此直接将其命名为《雨滴》
scenes.voice_spoken: When Sand asked him to listen to the rain falling from the eaves, Chopin denied that he was imitating the sounds of nature. Yet the insistent repeated note in this D-flat major prelude can sound like a pulse, or water that will never stop dripping. The work is now commonly known as the Raindrop Prelude.

scenes.title: 肖邦与雨滴
scenes.text: This is the Raindrop Prelude we are hearing today. Listen again to that repeated note. As the harmony darkens, how much weight does the same sound seem to carry?
scenes.text_zh: 我们今天听的是这首《雨滴》。现在再听那个重复的音。和声转暗了，同一声落下来，你会听成怎样的重量？
scenes.voice_spoken: This is the Raindrop Prelude we are hearing today. Listen again to that repeated note. As the harmony darkens, how much weight does the same sound seem to carry?

scenes.title: 革命与变革
scenes.text: Now turn the clock back to 1789. The French Revolution begins. People demand liberty, equality, and rights. From that year to the end of the Napoleonic era in 1815, twenty-six years pass. Revolution, coups, empire, and war carry this upheaval across Europe.
scenes.text_zh: 把时间拨回 1789 年。法国大革命爆发，人们要求自由、平等和权利。从这一年，到 1815 年拿破仑时代结束，是二十六年。法国大革命、革命之后的政变、帝国与战争又把这场巨变推向欧洲。
scenes.voice_spoken: Now turn the clock back to 1789. The French Revolution begins. People demand liberty, equality, and rights. From that year to the end of the Napoleonic era in 1815, twenty-six years pass. Revolution, coups, empire, and war carry this upheaval across Europe.

scenes.title: 革命与变革
scenes.text: In 1793, King Louis the Sixteenth is sent to the guillotine. During the Terror, arrests, trials, and executions become part of daily life.
scenes.text_zh: 1793 年，国王路易十六被送上断头台。恐怖时期，逮捕、审判和处决深入了日常生活。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1793, King Louis the Sixteenth is sent to the guillotine. During the Terror, arrests, trials, and executions become part of daily life.

scenes.title: 革命与变革
scenes.text: In 1794, as the Revolutionary Tribunal in Paris grows more extreme, Robespierre, a central figure of the Terror, is himself sent to the guillotine.
scenes.text_zh: 1794 年 伴随着巴黎革命法庭的极端化演变，恐怖统治的核心人物罗伯斯庇尔，自己也被送上了断头台。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1794, as the Revolutionary Tribunal in Paris grows more extreme, Robespierre, a central figure of the Terror, is himself sent to the guillotine.

scenes.title: 革命与变革
scenes.text: In 1799, Napoleon seizes power in a coup. In 1804, he crowns himself emperor. In 1815, after his defeat at Waterloo, he abdicates again. The Bourbon monarchy, overthrown by the Revolution, returns to France.
scenes.text_zh: 1799 年，拿破仑发动政变。1804 年，他加冕为皇帝。1815 年，滑铁卢战败，他再次退位。被革命推翻的波旁王朝，又回到了法国。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1799, Napoleon seizes power in a coup. In 1804, he crowns himself emperor. In 1815, after his defeat at Waterloo, he abdicates again. The Bourbon monarchy, overthrown by the Revolution, returns to France.

scenes.title: 革命与变革
scenes.text: Imagine growing from youth into middle age through all of this. You see a king fall, a republic emerge, a general become emperor, and finally a king return. Freedom has seemed close enough to touch. Tomorrow remains impossible to grasp. To understand Romanticism, we also need to understand that mixture of hope and unease.
scenes.text_zh: 想象一下，一个人从青年走到中年，看见王权倒下、共和国诞生、将军称帝，最后又看见国王回来。自由曾经近得像伸手就能碰到，明天却依然难以把握。理解浪漫主义，也要理解这份盼望和不安。
scenes.voice_spoken: Imagine growing from youth into middle age through all of this. You see a king fall, a republic emerge, a general become emperor, and finally a king return. Freedom has seemed close enough to touch. Tomorrow remains impossible to grasp. To understand Romanticism, we also need to understand that mixture of hope and unease.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 戈雅
scenes.text: Francisco Goya was a Spanish court painter. A serious illness in 1792 and 1793 left him deaf. For decades afterward, he continued to paint in a world he could no longer hear.
scenes.text_zh: 弗朗西斯科·戈雅，西班牙宫廷画家，1792 到 1793 年的一场重病让他失去了听力。往后几十年，他在一个自己听不见的世界里，继续作画。
scenes.voice_spoken: Francisco Goya was a Spanish court painter. A serious illness in 1792 and 1793 left him deaf. For decades afterward, he continued to paint in a world he could no longer hear.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 戈雅
scenes.text: In 1808, Madrid rose against the French occupation. The uprising was crushed. People were executed. Six years later, Goya painted two pictures about those two days.
scenes.text_zh: 1808 年，马德里反抗法军的占领。起义遭到镇压，有人被处决。六年后，他画了两幅关于这两天的画。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1808, Madrid rose against the French occupation. The uprising was crushed. People were executed. Six years later, Goya painted two pictures about those two days.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 戈雅
scenes.text: Look at The Third of May, 1808. A man in a white shirt kneels on the ground, his hands raised. The light reveals his eyes, and the people covering their faces beside him. Across from them, rifles are aimed. The soldiers' faces are almost invisible. Goya stops time at the instant these people face the guns.
scenes.text_zh: 看《1808 年 5 月 3 日》。白衫的人跪在地上，抬起双手。光照出他的眼睛，也照出身边捂脸的人。对面的枪口朝着他们，士兵的脸几乎看不见。在画上，他把时间停在这些人面对枪口的一刻。
scenes.voice_spoken: Look at The Third of May, 1808. A man in a white shirt kneels on the ground, his hands raised. The light reveals his eyes, and the people covering their faces beside him. Across from them, rifles are aimed. The soldiers' faces are almost invisible. Goya stops time at the instant these people face the guns.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 戈雅
scenes.text: Beyond this painting, he also made a series of prints later known as The Disasters of War. One shows civilians fleeing. Beneath it, he wrote a few words: I saw it.
scenes.text_zh: 他还做了一套版画，后来叫《战争的灾难》。有一张画着平民逃命，下面是他写的几个字：“我亲眼见过。”
scenes.voice_spoken: Beyond this painting, he also made a series of prints later known as The Disasters of War. One shows civilians fleeing. Beneath it, he wrote a few words: I saw it.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 籍里柯
scenes.text: Theodore Gericault was a French painter, born in Rouen. He loved riding and painted soldiers and horses. Later, his attention settled on a group of ordinary people abandoned at sea.
scenes.text_zh: 泰奥多尔·籍里柯，法国画家，出生在鲁昂，喜欢骑马，也画军人和马。他作画的目光后来停在一批被遗弃在海上的普通人身上。
scenes.voice_spoken: Theodore Gericault was a French painter, born in Rouen. He loved riding and painted soldiers and horses. Later, his attention settled on a group of ordinary people abandoned at sea.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 籍里柯
scenes.text: In 1816, the French naval vessel Medusa ran aground off the coast of West Africa. About a hundred and fifty people were left on a makeshift raft. Thirteen days later, fifteen were rescued at sea.
scenes.text_zh: 1816 年，法国军舰「梅杜萨」号在西非近海搁浅。约一百五十人被留在一只临时木筏上。漂流十三天后，十五人在海上获救。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1816, the French naval vessel Medusa ran aground off the coast of West Africa. About a hundred and fifty people were left on a makeshift raft. Thirteen days later, fifteen were rescued at sea.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 籍里柯
scenes.text: Gericault sought out survivors, built a model of the raft, and studied bodies in hospitals and a morgue. In 1819, this painting, more than seven metres wide, appeared at the Salon. Look toward the upper right. Someone has climbed as high as he can and waves a cloth toward the distance. On this enormous canvas, Gericault gives a lasting presence to people who were cast aside. The hope in that gesture belongs inside the painting, and beyond it.
scenes.text_zh: 籍里柯找过幸存者，做过木筏模型，也去医院和停尸房研究人的身体。1819 年，这幅长七米多的画在沙龙展出。看右上方，有人站到能站的最高处，朝远处挥布。他用巨大画幅，留下这些被抛下的人。那个挥布的动作所代表的希望就在画里，也在画面之外。
scenes.voice_spoken: Gericault sought out survivors, built a model of the raft, and studied bodies in hospitals and a morgue. In 1819, this painting, more than seven metres wide, appeared at the Salon. Look toward the upper right. Someone has climbed as high as he can and waves a cloth toward the distance. On this enormous canvas, Gericault gives a lasting presence to people who were cast aside. The hope in that gesture belongs inside the painting, and beyond it.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 德拉克洛瓦
scenes.text: Eugene Delacroix was a leading French Romantic painter of the nineteenth century. Trained in Paris as a young man, he lived through changes of political power.
scenes.text_zh: 欧仁·德拉克洛瓦是十九世纪法国浪漫主义的重要画家，年轻时在巴黎接受绘画训练，亲眼经历了政权更迭。
scenes.voice_spoken: Eugene Delacroix was a leading French Romantic painter of the nineteenth century. Trained in Paris as a young man, he lived through changes of political power.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 德拉克洛瓦
scenes.text: Paris, 1830. On July twenty-sixth, King Charles the Tenth restricts the press, dissolves the newly elected Chamber of Deputies, and changes the electoral rules. Journalists protest. Barricades rise in the streets. The uprising of July twenty-seventh through twenty-ninth becomes known as the Three Glorious Days. Charles the Tenth abdicates.
scenes.text_zh: 1830 年的巴黎。7 月 26 日，国王查理十世限制新闻出版，解散刚选出的众议院，也改变选举规则。巴黎的记者发表抗议，街头接着筑起街垒。7 月 27 日到 29 日的起义被称为“光荣三日”。查理十世退位。
scenes.voice_spoken: Paris, 1830. On July twenty-sixth, King Charles the Tenth restricts the press, dissolves the newly elected Chamber of Deputies, and changes the electoral rules. Journalists protest. Barricades rise in the streets. The uprising of July twenty-seventh through twenty-ninth becomes known as the Three Glorious Days. Charles the Tenth abdicates.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 德拉克洛瓦
scenes.text: Why did Delacroix paint this picture? Even if I did not fight for my country, I can still celebrate it through my paintings.
scenes.text_zh: 德拉克洛瓦为什么画，这幅画？“即使我没有为了我的祖国战斗，我也可以用我的画作来歌颂它。”
scenes.voice_spoken: Why did Delacroix paint this picture? Even if I did not fight for my country, I can still celebrate it through my paintings.

scenes.title: 社会事件 · 德拉克洛瓦
scenes.text: The painting contains a real Paris: Notre-Dame in the smoke. At the front, a woman raises the tricolour. She embodies a freedom that can move, and lead people across the barricades. The crowd follows her, advancing toward us.
scenes.text_zh: 画里有真实的巴黎。烟雾的巴黎圣母院，一位举三色旗的女子走在前面，她代表了一个能迈步、能带人跨过街垒的人，人群跟着她朝我们前进。
scenes.voice_spoken: The painting contains a real Paris: Notre-Dame in the smoke. At the front, a woman raises the tricolour. She embodies a freedom that can move, and lead people across the barricades. The crowd follows her, advancing toward us.

scenes.title: 自然 · 约瑟夫·赖特
scenes.text: Joseph Wright, of Derby in eighteenth-century England, often painted scientific experiments, craftspeople, and scholars. His circle included people interested in industry and new knowledge. He knew how to place a single light in the darkness, and show how people gathered around it.
scenes.text_zh: 约瑟夫·赖特，十八世纪英国德比的画家，常画科学实验、工匠与学者，身边有不少关心工业和新知识的人。他擅长在黑暗中安排一道光，看人怎样围着它。
scenes.voice_spoken: Joseph Wright, of Derby in eighteenth-century England, often painted scientific experiments, craftspeople, and scholars. His circle included people interested in industry and new knowledge. He knew how to place a single light in the darkness, and show how people gathered around it.

scenes.title: 自然 · 约瑟夫·赖特
scenes.text: In 1774, Wright visited Vesuvius and called it the most astonishing sight in nature. In this painting of an eruption, look first at the fire. It lights the crater and the clouds of smoke. Then look at the bay. The moonlight is cold. The sea remains still. The people on the shore are so small that you can almost miss them.
scenes.text_zh: 1774 年，赖特去看维苏威火山，称那是“自然界最惊人的景象”。这幅《维苏威火山喷发》，先看火光，它把山口和烟云烧成亮色。再看海湾，月光很冷，海面仍然很静。岸边那几个人小得几乎要找不到。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1774, Wright visited Vesuvius and called it the most astonishing sight in nature. In this painting of an eruption, look first at the fire. It lights the crater and the clouds of smoke. Then look at the bay. The moonlight is cold. The sea remains still. The people on the shore are so small that you can almost miss them.

scenes.title: 自然 · 约瑟夫·赖特
scenes.text: We stand before the painting, drawn to the fire, and discover how fragile its people are. Danger, attraction, and human smallness enter a single act of looking. This experience later becomes one way into the Romantic idea of the sublime.
scenes.text_zh: 我们站在画前看火光，也发现画里的人小得那样脆弱。危险、吸引和人的微小，同时进入一次观看。这种体验，后来成为理解浪漫主义“崇高”的一个入口。
scenes.voice_spoken: We stand before the painting, drawn to the fire, and discover how fragile its people are. Danger, attraction, and human smallness enter a single act of looking. This experience later becomes one way into the Romantic idea of the sublime.

scenes.title: 自然 · 弗里德里希
scenes.text: Caspar David Friedrich was born in Greifswald, on the Baltic coast, and later spent much of his life painting landscapes in Dresden. He lost his mother at seven. When he was thirteen, his brother drowned in an accident on the ice. Loss entered his life very early.
scenes.text_zh: 卡斯帕·大卫·弗里德里希，出生在波罗的海岸边的格赖夫斯瓦尔德，后来长期在德累斯顿画风景。他七岁失去母亲，十三岁那年，弟弟在一次冰上事故中溺亡。对他来说，失去很早就进入了生活。
scenes.voice_spoken: Caspar David Friedrich was born in Greifswald, on the Baltic coast, and later spent much of his life painting landscapes in Dresden. He lost his mother at seven. When he was thirteen, his brother drowned in an accident on the ice. Loss entered his life very early.

scenes.title: 自然 · 弗里德里希
scenes.text: His demand was direct: paint what you see before you, and what you see within. A landscape passes through someone's eyes, and through someone's life. It carries the weight of that encounter.
scenes.text_zh: 他的要求很直接，画眼前所见，也要画内心所见。一个景色经过谁的眼睛、谁的一生，最后就会带着怎样的分量。
scenes.voice_spoken: His demand was direct: paint what you see before you, and what you see within. A landscape passes through someone's eyes, and through someone's life. It carries the weight of that encounter.

scenes.title: 自然 · 弗里德里希
scenes.text: Look at Monk by the Sea. The shore lies low. Beyond it is a dark sea. A vast sky surrounds the small figure beneath it. Describing the painting, Friedrich suggested that even thinking from morning until night cannot reveal the mystery of the distant beyond. Visible immensity and human limitation enter the same seascape.
scenes.text_zh: 看《海边的修道士》。岸被画得很低，远处是暗海，大片天空把那个人围在下面。弗里德里希描述这幅画时说，即使从清晨想到深夜，人依然难以参透那神秘的彼岸。看得见的辽阔，和人的有限，一起进入了这幅海景。
scenes.voice_spoken: Look at Monk by the Sea. The shore lies low. Beyond it is a dark sea. A vast sky surrounds the small figure beneath it. Describing the painting, Friedrich suggested that even thinking from morning until night cannot reveal the mystery of the distant beyond. Visible immensity and human limitation enter the same seascape.

scenes.title: 自然 · 弗里德里希
scenes.text: Now look at Wanderer above the Sea of Fog. The rocks nearby are sharply visible. Only fragments of the way ahead can be seen. This person has reached a high place, yet so much before him remains unclear. Standing higher can also reveal the limits of our sight.
scenes.text_zh: 再看《雾海上的旅人》。近处的岩石清清楚楚，前面的路只露出一点。那个人已经走到了高处，眼前仍然有很多看不清的地方。站得更高，也会让我们更清楚地发现自己目光的边界。
scenes.label_en: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
scenes.voice_spoken: Now look at Wanderer above the Sea of Fog. The rocks nearby are sharply visible. Only fragments of the way ahead can be seen. This person has reached a high place, yet so much before him remains unclear. Standing higher can also reveal the limits of our sight.

scenes.title: 自然 · 透纳
scenes.text: Joseph Mallord William Turner was the son of a London barber. His father once displayed his pictures in the shop window to sell them. Turner later entered the Royal Academy, travelled, and sketched. Sea, weather, and light became the work of a lifetime.
scenes.text_zh: 约瑟夫·马洛德·威廉·透纳，是英国伦敦一位理发师的儿子。父亲曾把他的画挂在店铺橱窗里卖。后来他进入皇家美术学院，旅行、写生，把海、天气和光作为一生的题材。
scenes.voice_spoken: Joseph Mallord William Turner was the son of a London barber. His father once displayed his pictures in the shop window to sell them. Turner later entered the Royal Academy, travelled, and sketched. Sea, weather, and light became the work of a lifetime.

scenes.title: 自然 · 透纳
scenes.text: In 1838, the old warship Temeraire was towed away by a steam tug to be broken up. A year later, Turner painted that last journey.
scenes.text_zh: 1838 年，老战舰「特梅雷尔」号被蒸汽拖船拉去拆解。一年后，透纳把这趟航程画下来。
scenes.voice_spoken: In 1838, the old warship Temeraire was towed away by a steam tug to be broken up. A year later, Turner painted that last journey.

scenes.title: 自然 · 透纳
scenes.text: In a draft letter, Turner called this painting his darling. People offered to buy it, but he never sold it. He eventually left it to the nation. The old ship went to the breakers. The painter preserved its last image.
scenes.text_zh: 透纳在一封信稿里把这幅画叫作自己的“宝贝”。有人出钱要买，他始终没有卖。最后他把画留给了国家。旧舰走向拆解，画家把它最后的形象留了下来。
scenes.voice_spoken: In a draft letter, Turner called this painting his darling. People offered to buy it, but he never sold it. He eventually left it to the nation. The old ship went to the breakers. The painter preserved its last image.

scenes.title: 自然 · 透纳
scenes.text: Then, in 1844, he painted a steam train. The diagonal of the bridge reaches straight toward us. Its engine emerges through rain and mist. Think of the old sailing ship we have just seen. Change brings power, and also carries familiar things away. We may keep pace with it, and still need time to feel what it has taken.
scenes.text_zh: 到 1844 年，他又画了一列蒸汽火车。桥的斜线直朝我们伸来，车头从雨雾里出现。想想刚才那艘旧帆船。变化会带来力量，也会让熟悉的东西离开。一个人跟得上它，还要有时间去感觉它带走了什么。
scenes.voice_spoken: Then, in 1844, he painted a steam train. The diagonal of the bridge reaches straight toward us. Its engine emerges through rain and mist. Think of the old sailing ship we have just seen. Change brings power, and also carries familiar things away. We may keep pace with it, and still need time to feel what it has taken.

scenes.title: 感受
scenes.text: Sand heard rain on the roof. Chopin felt drops falling on his chest. The same rain carries a different weight in each person's inner world. Music lets someone else approach that feeling.
scenes.text_zh: 桑听见屋瓦上的雨，肖邦感到胸口的水滴。同一场雨，在各自心里有不同的分量。音乐使另一个人也能接近那份感受。
scenes.label_zh: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.voice_spoken: Sand heard rain on the roof. Chopin felt drops falling on his chest. The same rain carries a different weight in each person's inner world. Music lets someone else approach that feeling.

scenes.title: 自然
scenes.text: Volcanoes, seas, and fog change in their own ways. They draw us in, and can frighten us. We live within them. Our sight and our power have limits.
scenes.text_zh: 火山、大海和雾有自己的变化。人会被它们吸引，也会害怕。我们生活在其中，目光和力量都有边界。
scenes.label_zh: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.voice_spoken: Volcanoes, seas, and fog change in their own ways. They draw us in, and can frighten us. We live within them. Our sight and our power have limits.

scenes.title: 时间
scenes.text: A ship departs. A generation passes. A painting can bring that moment to people who come later.
scenes.text_zh: 一艘船离开了，一代人过去了。画可以把那一刻带给后来的人。
scenes.label_zh: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.voice_spoken: A ship departs. A generation passes. A painting can bring that moment to people who come later.

scenes.title: 人的有限性
scenes.text: The hand is already raised. The distant ship has not yet answered. Between what we can do and what will happen, there is often a stretch of waiting. The painter leaves that distance in the picture.
scenes.text_zh: 那只手已经举起，远处的船还没有回应。人能做的和结果之间，往往还有一段等待。画家把这段距离留在了画里。
scenes.label_zh: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.voice_spoken: The hand is already raised. The distant ship has not yet answered. Between what we can do and what will happen, there is often a stretch of waiting. The painter leaves that distance in the picture.

scenes.title: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.text: When so much is changing, we want to know what comes next, right away. When we cannot know, anxiety and worry follow. Romantic artists did not remain in sorrow over human limits. They reached for moments that could endure.
scenes.text_zh: 面对太多变化，我们会想马上知道下一刻，如果不知道，我们就会焦虑，担忧。浪漫主义艺术家们没有停留在人的有限里悲伤，而是抓住永恒的瞬间。
scenes.label_zh: 感受 · 自然 · 时间 · 人的有限性
scenes.voice_spoken: When so much is changing, we want to know what comes next, right away. When we cannot know, anxiety and worry follow. Romantic artists did not remain in sorrow over human limits. They reached for moments that could endure.

scenes.title: 开头的旋律回来了
scenes.text: It is still the same repeated note, and the opening melody has returned. Do you hear worry about the unknown, or a quietness that comes from recognising our limits? We can listen slowly, and take time to think.
scenes.text_zh: 还是同一个重复的音，开头那条旋律回来了。你听到的是因未知而担忧，还是因认识到自己的有限而平静？我们可以慢慢听一听，想一想。
scenes.voice_spoken: It is still the same repeated note, and the opening melody has returned. Do you hear worry about the unknown, or a quietness that comes from recognising our limits? We can listen slowly, and take time to think.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: A small closing surprise: mono no aware, a literary and aesthetic sensibility with roots in Japan's Heian period. Mono refers to the things of this world: flowers, birds, wind, moonlight, and the changes of human life. Aware was an exclamation, an ah of feeling. It names a heartfelt response, a deep resonance with what we encounter. That response can include joy, wonder, compassion, and a gentle sadness.
scenes.text_zh: 片尾彩蛋：日本平安时代孕育出的核心文学与美学理念，物哀Mono no aware ，“物”（Mono）指世间万事万物（如花鸟风月、人事无常）；“哀”（Aware，古日语叹词“啊华雷”）是指面对客观万物时，内心所发出的由衷感叹、深切共鸣与赞叹，包含喜悦、惊叹、怜悯与淡淡的感伤。
scenes.voice_spoken: A small closing surprise: mono no ah-wah-ray, a literary and aesthetic sensibility with roots in Japan's Heian period. Mono refers to the things of this world: flowers, birds, wind, moonlight, and the changes of human life. Aware was an exclamation, an ah of feeling. It names a heartfelt response, a deep resonance with what we encounter. That response can include joy, wonder, compassion, and a gentle sadness.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: The most beautiful things are often fleeting: falling cherry blossoms, a waning moon, a bud just opening. Because a life, or a thing, will pass away, its moment of radiance moves us all the more.
scenes.text_zh: 最美的事物往往是短暂易逝的,如樱花飘落、残月、初绽的蓓蕾，正因为生命或事物会消逝，其当下的闪光才格外动。
scenes.voice_spoken: The most beautiful things are often fleeting: falling cherry blossoms, a waning moon, a bud just opening. Because a life, or a thing, will pass away, its moment of radiance moves us all the more.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: An attachment to what will not last.
scenes.text_zh: 对短暂之物的留恋。
scenes.voice_spoken: An attachment to what will not last.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: We can follow this path to look at mono no aware, alongside Romanticism.
scenes.text_zh: 我们可以沿这条路一起看物哀美学，与浪漫主义。
scenes.voice_spoken: We can follow this path to look at mono no ah-wah-ray, alongside Romanticism.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: We feel affection for what unfolds before us, because we know we cannot hold on to it.
scenes.text_zh: 对眼前发生的一切，人会感到眷恋，因为知道自己留不住它。
scenes.voice_spoken: We feel affection for what unfolds before us, because we know we cannot hold on to it.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: When something slips beyond our grasp, what remains in your heart? Pressure and anxiety? Romantic feeling and peace? Or wonder and joy?
scenes.text_zh: 面对抓不住、留不住的东西，你留在心里的是压力，焦虑呢？
scenes.voice_spoken: When something slips beyond our grasp, what remains in your heart? Pressure and anxiety? Romantic feeling and peace? Or wonder and joy?

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: It is not a choice of one out of three.
scenes.text_zh: 是浪漫，平静呢？
scenes.voice_spoken: It is not a choice of one out of three.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: Or two out of six.
scenes.text_zh: 还是赞叹，喜悦呢？
scenes.voice_spoken: Or two out of six.

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: Would you simply be willing to give your heart a little more room, and look a little longer?
scenes.text_zh: 不是三选一，也不是六选二，只是你愿意把心放宽一些，多看看嘛？
scenes.voice_spoken: Would you simply be willing to give your heart a little more room, and look a little longer?

scenes.title: 片尾彩蛋 · 物哀
scenes.text: That is what these Romantic artists were doing.
scenes.text_zh: 这就是浪漫主义艺术家做的事情。
scenes.voice_spoken: That is what these Romantic artists were doing.
